subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Room That Stabilized at 6.5 mg/m³, Not 0.2
featured_title: THE ROOM THAT STABILIZED AT 6.5 MG PER CUBIC METER, NOT 0.2

presentation.challenge: Dividing generation by room volume produced a concentration rise rate. The steady indoor concentration was controlled by ventilation and reached 6.5 mg/m³.

practice.primary_question: How is steady indoor pollutant concentration calculated from pollutant generation, ventilation, and outdoor concentration?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Dividing pollutant generation by room volume and reporting the resulting concentration-per-time as a steady concentration.

case_dna.target_misconception: A pollutant source of 60 mg/min in a 300 m³ room gives a steady concentration of 60/300=0.2 mg/m³.
case_dna.why_plausible: Generation divided by volume looks like a concentration, but its units are actually mg/(m³·min), a concentration rise rate.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: At steady state with Q=10 m³/min and outdoor concentration 0.5 mg/m³, QCin+G=QC gives C=0.5+60/10=6.5 mg/m³.
case_dna.corrected_model: For a well-mixed room with no decay or deposition, steady concentration is C=Cin+G/Q. Room volume affects transient response time, not this steady-state concentration.

problem_statement: A well-mixed 300 m³ room contains a pollutant source emitting 60 mg/min. Outdoor air enters at 10 m³/min with pollutant concentration 0.5 mg/m³, and an equal flow leaves the room. Neglect decay and deposition. A note divides 60 by 300 and reports 0.2 mg/m³ as the steady indoor concentration. Determine the correct steady-state concentration.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The volume calculation produced a rate, not a steady concentration.
gates.prompt: At steady state, what flow carries pollutant out of the room?
gates.cta: Balance inflow plus generation against outflow

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Choose the correct steady-state room balance

options.label: Use QCin+G=QC, so C=Cin+G/Q
options.reason: At steady state, pollutant mass entering plus generation equals pollutant mass leaving.

options.label: Use C=G/V
options.reason: G/V has units of concentration per time, not concentration.

options.label: Use C=Cin-G/Q
options.reason: An internal source raises indoor concentration above the incoming concentration.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Run the well-mixed room to steady state
gates.result: The steady indoor concentration is 6.5 mg/m³.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the steady concentration
gates.hint: At steady state, the source term is balanced by ventilation outflow.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Ventilation sets the steady source contribution

cards.text: Total pollutant entering or generated=5+60=65 mg/min.
At steady state, 10C=65, so C=6.5 mg/m³.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the indoor-air note
report: C1. The room volume is 300 m³.
C3. Therefore steady concentration is 60/300=0.2 mg/m³.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated room volume.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated source rate.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The units are mg/(m³·min), and ventilation was omitted from the steady-state balance.

evidence_choices.label: 10(0.5)+60=10C gives C=6.5 mg/m³
evidence_choices.reason: This is the steady well-mixed mass balance.

correction.template: The steady indoor pollutant concentration is {concentration} mg/m³.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Hold the room at or below 2.5 mg/m³
gates.constraint: Keep G=60 mg/min and Cin=0.5 mg/m³.

options.label: Provide at least 30 m³/min of ventilation
Keep 10 m³/min
options.reason: That leaves the concentration at 6.5 mg/m³.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same room model at higher ventilation
gates.prompt: If Q=20 m³/min with the same source and outdoor concentration, what is steady C?

options.label: 6.5 mg/m³
options.reason: That is the result at 10 m³/min.

options.label: 0.2 mg/m³
options.reason: That repeats the volume-based unit error.

gates.explanation: With no decay, the source contribution at steady state is G/Q.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the indoor-air mass balance
gates.confirmation: I confirm that steady indoor concentration is determined by pollutant generation and ventilation, while room volume primarily affects transient response for this model.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A concentration rise rate was mistaken for steady concentration.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: For the stated steady well-mixed model, use C=Cin+G/Q.

seo.seo_title: Indoor Air Steady-State Mass Balance | FE Environmental E-075
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-075: a 60 mg/min source with 10 m³/min ventilation and 0.5 mg/m³ outdoor air gives 6.5 mg/m³ indoors.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental indoor air steady state mass balance
seo.excerpt: Generation divided by room volume is not a steady concentration. Ventilation controls the steady pollutant level in a well-mixed room.
seo.direct_answer: At steady state, QCin+G=QC. With Cin=0.5 mg/m³, G=60 mg/min, and Q=10 m³/min, C=0.5+60/10=6.5 mg/m³.
